Hydraulic HosesMay 18, 20265 min read

By YRVIMAR Technical Team

Preventive maintenance of industrial hoses

A hose that fails can cost more than the equipment. An inspection routine to anticipate failures and extend service life.

Hoses are consumables, but that doesn't mean they should fail without warning. A simple preventive maintenance program reduces downtime, accidents and costs. Here's a routine you can apply in any workshop or operation.

Periodic visual inspection

At least once per shift on critical equipment, check for:

  • Cracks, blisters or worn cover.
  • Leaks at the fittings (never with your hand: use cardboard).
  • Exposed or corroded steel reinforcement.
  • Twisted, crushed or edge-rubbing hoses.

Date and pressure control

Log the installation date. Many failures come from exceeding the recommended service life. Verify that the actual working pressure does not exceed the hose's rating.

Routing and protection

80% of premature wear comes from poor routing: tight bends, rubbing and torsion. Use guides, protective spring guards and respect the minimum bend radius.

Correct storage

Store spare hoses in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. PVC and rubber degrade with heat and UV, which is relevant in Panama's climate.

Safety first

Install whip check cables on pressurized air and water lines. In case of a hydraulic fluid leak, depressurize before working: a high-pressure jet can penetrate skin.
